doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Jazz's role today and Dizzy Gillespie
summary: Goodwin says people will keep playing jazz; he recalls touring with Dizzy and playing at the Deer Head Inn.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well from Herb Alpert to — Yeah, all these people. It’s amazing. One last thing and I don’t know if I can formulate this question so that you could try to answer it. Does jazz have a role in society now? I feel like it used to and I’m wondering if it still does in your opinion?

I was going to ask you what you think, but I think that as long as people love that music they’re going to want to play it. It’s not about the bread or any of that. I mean there’s plenty of opportunities in commercial music to play good music. But to play jazz, especially the stuff that I like which is straight ahead jazz, you know bebop essentially, but you know I don’t just play bop but we played good bebop with Phil and that was fantastic for me. I knew all the repertoire, and then we got to record and tour with Dizzy Gillespie with the quintet, it was the highlight of my life you know, because Dizzy had been my idol since I was about 13, one of the main idols and so to get to know him and to work with him was great and to have the friendships with all these great players went beyond playing together but it involved playing together, it involved knowing each other, hanging out and doing fun things. I wish I could remember more of it. I think it will always be there man, I really do. Because as long as people want to play it, we’ll play it for fun, for ourselves. We’ll get together and play. I play one night a week at the Deer Head Inn, you know, it’s a jazz outpost that’s become more well known, especially because of the Keith Jarrett recordings, which I produced by the way.
